user_goal: Make Plotkeeper release-contract selection explicit, deterministic, and fail closed across the trusted host guard and server-side verifier, so non-release successor contracts can never unlock or supersede the designated public-release contract.

authority.verbatim_text: Create append-only production contract successor (baseline 9d0400f) authorizing only trusted guard/server verifier/workflow/config/tests/docs/checkpoints/new contract. Current flaw: trusted guard latest_active_contract chooses newest mtime; newest listener ownership contract has RL-NONE/no release, while workflow verifier designates v017-pr-release. Make release contract selection explicit/deterministic and fail closed; non-release successors must never unlock or supersede release. Prefer a repository tracked pointer/designated contract that host guard and server verifier agree on, and test mtime/reordering/adversarial non-release successor. Do not commit/push/install/live mutate. Run focused/full tests, verifier/guard adversarial, diff check. Return exact files/hashes/evidence. No children.

baseline.protection_evidence: Clean single worktree at the exact delegated release-surface head before this successor contract or implementation mutation.
baseline.selection_reason: The delegation explicitly names 9d0400f as the protected baseline and limits the repair to release-contract authority selection and its proof surfaces.

resources: Tracked release-contract pointer and disposable temporary repositories/contract fixtures used by tests only.
semantic_changes: Resolve one tracked designated release contract by an explicit relative path and content hash, shared by the host guard and server verifier.
Reject missing, malformed, absolute, traversal, hash-mismatched, non-ACTIVE, or non-release designated contracts before any release command is authorized.
Keep workflow configuration on the same tracked pointer and add adversarial mtime/reordering and non-release-successor proof without installation, service, commit, push, or deployment mutation.

paths: any path not explicitly listed under allowed.paths
semantic_changes: No release, merge, push, install, restart, deployment, live-process, listener, connector, ledger, UI, database, dependency, or user-project behavior change.
No filesystem mtime, filename ordering, newest-contract heuristic, environment-only override, or non-release contract may authorize or supersede the designated release contract.
No pointer or contract fixture may escape the repository root or be treated as release authority without exact pointer identity and content-hash agreement.

invariants: The host guard and server verifier resolve the same tracked designated release contract and exact contract-file SHA-256.
A newer or reordered ACTIVE successor with RL-NONE cannot unlock, supersede, or change the selected release contract.
Missing, malformed, tampered, path-traversing, non-ACTIVE, or non-release pointers fail closed.
The current v0.1.7 public-release contract remains the designated target until a separately authorized pointer change is reviewed.
The worktree remains free of installation, live-service, commit, push, and deployment mutation.

acceptance_cases.promised_behavior: The guard and verifier select the tracked designated release contract by explicit path, contract ID, and exact content hash rather than mtime or directory order.
acceptance_cases.forbidden_behavior: Selecting the newest ACTIVE JSON, accepting an unbound environment override, or allowing guard/verifier disagreement.
acceptance_cases.target_and_actor: Plotkeeper host release guard and server-side public-release verifier

acceptance_cases.promised_behavior: A newer, reordered, or adversarial ACTIVE non-release successor with RL-NONE cannot unlock or supersede the designated public-release contract.
acceptance_cases.forbidden_behavior: Release authorization changing because of mtime, filename order, pointer tampering, or a non-release successor.
acceptance_cases.target_and_actor: Disposable contract fixtures and release decision paths

acceptance_cases.promised_behavior: Only the authorized trust, workflow, documentation, test, pointer, contract, and checkpoint surfaces change and all focused/full validation passes.
acceptance_cases.forbidden_behavior: Unlisted diffs, release operations, installation, live-service mutation, commit, push, or skipped adversarial proof.
acceptance_cases.target_and_actor: Protected 9d0400f checkout and local validation commands

proof_requirements.claim: Static and unit proof show both trust paths consume one tracked pointer and reject pointer/contract identity or hash disagreement.
proof_requirements.required_environment: Protected Plotkeeper checkout with no installation or live-service mutation
proof_requirements.command_or_read_only_check: Focused guard and verifier tests plus workflow/docs pointer assertions
proof_requirements.expected_observation: Guard and verifier resolve the same exact designated release contract; malformed or mismatched inputs are denied.

proof_requirements.claim: Disposable fixtures prove mtime/reordering and adversarial non-release successors cannot unlock or supersede release authority.
proof_requirements.command_or_read_only_check: Focused adversarial unittest cases exercising guard and verifier selection
proof_requirements.expected_observation: The designated release path remains stable and non-release/tampered pointers fail closed.

proof_requirements.claim: The exact allowed diff is bounded and the repository remains regression-free.
proof_requirements.command_or_read_only_check: Contract validation, focused tests, full unittest suite, Python syntax, workflow/doc assertions, and git diff --check
proof_requirements.expected_observation: All checks pass; no forbidden path or operational mutation appears.

release_requirements.required_receipt: No release or deployment is authorized in this bounded repair lane; parent v0.1.7 release review remains required.

stop_conditions: Any unexpected diff, pointer/hash disagreement, failed focused/full test, syntax or diff-check failure, or inability to prove guard/verifier agreement.
Any request to commit, push, install, restart, deploy, mutate live service, or broaden the allowed surfaces without a new append-only contract.
known_discrepancies: The listener-ownership successor is newer and intentionally RL-NONE; it must remain independent of public-release authority.
The workflow previously named the release contract directly; this repair replaces that duplicate authority with the tracked pointer while preserving the same designated target.
